summary: I read the sample under app/. A working Python sample is present: it connects to a DocumentDB cluster via DOCUMENTDB_URI, seeds an idempotent dataset, creates indexes, attempts a server-side $graphLookup and falls back to a bounded client-side traversal, applies AML heuristics, and emits structured Pydantic SuspiciousChain objects. The build ran seed and detector against the live cluster in this environment. Important gaps: the typology matching was not implemented as server-side aggregation stages (the detection logic runs in Python), a single shared MongoClient singleton was not implemented, tests require a live cluster (no offline unit tests), and some dependency versions are not fully pinned. Also, external documentation was not searchable from this run (documentation_search_available=false), so many external best-practice checks could not be verified beyond the local code. See requirement_results, checks and doc_gaps for details and minimal fixes.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the agent in Python with LangChain as a single agent that is given a DocumentDB aggregation tool and invokes that tool to analyse transactions.
requirement_results.evidence: src/detector.py defines AggregationTool that the CLI uses (src/run_detector.py lines 7-12) but there is no LangChain AgentExecutor or agent orchestration that loads this tool as a LangChain tool.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a tiny example that registers AggregationTool as a LangChain Tool and runs an AgentExecutor (one file with a few lines showing Tool/AgentExecutor usage), or add an example function in run_detector.py demonstrating using LangChain to call the tool.

requirement_results.requirement: The DocumentDB aggregation tool runs aggregation pipelines against the transaction documents in Azure DocumentDB through a MongoDB driver (e.g. PyMongo's `aggregate`).
requirement_results.evidence: src/detector.py uses a PyMongo aggregation pipeline (lines ~34-46) and calls list(self.tx.aggregate(pipeline)). Requirements pin pymongo==4.4.0 (app/requirements.txt line 1).

requirement_results.requirement: Transactions are modelled as documents that reference other documents (e.g. a counterparty account or a linked transaction), and the aggregation tool follows those references to assemble counterparty chains (e.g. with `$graphLookup` or chained `$lookup` stages).
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed_data.py creates transaction documents with fields _id, from_account, to_account, timestamp (e.g. lines ~35-46). src/detector.py implements follow_chain using $graphLookup when supported (lines ~34-45) and a client-side BFS fallback (lines ~54-70).

requirement_results.requirement: Known AML typology rules are expressed as stages of the aggregation pipeline, so the typology matching runs in Azure DocumentDB (e.g. circular transfers, structuring just below a threshold, rapid pass-through of funds).
requirement_results.evidence: Detector applies rules in Python within detect_suspicious (src/detector.py lines ~72-128): structuring, rapid pass-through and cycle detection are implemented by Python queries and logic rather than as aggregation pipeline stages executed server-side.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Move the heuristic computations into aggregation stages returned by the aggregation tool (e.g., construct a pipeline that $graphLookup -> $unwind/$group to compute tx_count, total_amount, time_span, and $match on thresholds) and return only flagged chains from the tool.

requirement_results.requirement: Chains that match a typology rule are flagged as suspicious, and the flagged chains are what the tool returns to the agent.
requirement_results.evidence: detect_suspicious builds SuspiciousChain objects when reasons exist and returns them; examples printed by python -m src.run_detector are the serialized flagged chains (events.jsonl run output). See src/detector.py lines ~118-128 and src/run_detector.py lines ~7-12.

requirement_results.requirement: For each flagged chain the agent generates a structured suspicious activity narrative: an object with defined fields (e.g. a Pydantic model or JSON) that describes the chain and the suspicious pattern it matched.
requirement_results.evidence: src/detector.py defines SuspiciousChain as a Pydantic model (lines ~18-24) and populates narrative via _generate_narrative (lines ~130-148). The CLI prints JSON (src/run_detector.py lines ~7-12).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY (app/.env.example lines 4-7); src/db.py reads DOCUMENTDB_URI via os.getenv (lines ~9-16). No secrets are committed in the repo.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example contains DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY and DB_NAME (lines 4-10).

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: This sample does not create vector indexes or call an embedding model; no vector-index code is present in the repo.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If vector search will be added, add explicit embedding-dimension constants and verify index creation uses that dimension; include a short test that validates dimension consistency.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector index code or parameter guidance in the repository.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Only applicable if the sample includes vector search: add index-parameter guidance and examples in README and the seed/index script.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: src/db.py get_client() constructs a new MongoClient on each call (lines ~13-19). The CLI calls get_db() once for a single run, but other code paths call get_db() separately (seed_data and run_detector each call get_db()), so there is no module-level shared client singleton.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Create a module-level client in src/db.py (e.g., instantiate MongoClient once on first call and cache it) and have get_client()/get_db reuse that client.

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: src/seed_data.py creates indexes in ensure_indexes (lines ~7-13), inserts accounts and uses replace_one(..., upsert=True) for transactions (lines ~47-52) and uses a metadata marker to skip rerun (lines ~18-21 and 51-52).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample does not implement a /search web endpoint.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Not applicable unless a search endpoint is added; then validate empty-query behavior and embed-failure handling.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search endpoint or vector similarity code present in the repo.
app/requirements.txt pins pymongo==4.4.0, pydantic==1.10.11, python-dotenv==1.0.0 but uses openai>=1.0.0 and langchain>=0.0.200 (lines 1-5).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin openai and langchain to tested versions (replace >= with exact versions) and run a quick install to verify compatibility.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: tests/test_seed_and_detect.py is explicitly skipped if DOCUMENTDB_URI is not set (tests/test_seed_and_detect.py line 7); it requires a live cluster to run.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a separate unit-test module that uses a mocking library (e.g., mongomock or patching MongoClient) so tests can run offline and deterministically.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC (Bicep/Terraform/ARM) files are present and README explicitly states the sample expects an existing cluster and does not provision one.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add optional IaC snippets (Bicep/Terraform) as examples (clearly marked optional) using the appropriate Azure resource type; include a note the sample runs against an existing cluster by default.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: README.md documents what the sample shows, prerequisites and quickstart run steps (app/README.md lines ~5-13 and ~32-47) but does not include explicit clean-up steps (no drop/teardown guidance).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a short 'clean-up' section to README that explains how to remove seed data (e.g., commands to drop the sample_banking_01 database or delete sample collections).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: README and .env.example refer to 'DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible)' / 'Azure DocumentDB' consistently (app/README.md line 1 and lines ~7). No mention of a neighbouring product was found.

checks.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string from the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable at runtime and provide a .env.example placeholder rather than committing credentials.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example lines 1-7; src/db.py lines 7-16 (load_dotenv and os.getenv('DOCUMENTDB_URI')).

checks.practice: Seed sample data idempotently using replace_one(..., upsert=True) for each seeded document and mark seeding completion with a dedicated metadata document to avoid duplicate seeds on re-run.
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py lines ~47-52 use db.transactions.replace_one(..., upsert=True) and meta.replace_one(..., upsert=True); seed checks meta.find_one({'sample_seeded': True}) (lines ~18-21).

checks.practice: Create single-field indexes on transactions for fields used in traversal and filtering (from_account, to_account, timestamp) and a unique index on accounts.account_id before running queries.
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py ensure_indexes creates idx_from_account, idx_to_account, idx_timestamp and idx_account_id unique on accounts (lines ~7-13).

checks.practice: Detect whether the server supports $graphLookup by issuing a minimal aggregation with explain and, if unsupported, fall back to a client-side traversal implementation.
checks.evidence: src/db.py supports_graph_lookup runs an aggregate with explain (lines ~36-48) and src/detector.py uses supports_graph_lookup result (line ~30) to choose pipeline vs client-side BFS.

checks.practice: When using $graphLookup in aggregation pipelines, set maxDepth to limit recursion and bound server-side graph traversal work.
Implement a bounded client-side BFS traversal fallback that tracks visited transaction IDs and limits hops to avoid unbounded in-memory expansion and cycles.
checks.evidence: src/detector.py client-side fallback uses visited set, queue and hops limit (lines ~54-70).

checks.practice: Use projection (e.g., $project) in aggregation pipelines to return only the necessary fields (for example, project only the assembled 'chain') to reduce network and memory use.
Use aggregate explain (or explain-mode aggregation) to validate whether certain aggregation operators are accepted by the server without scanning or requiring actual data.
checks.evidence: src/db.py supports_graph_lookup calls db.command({'aggregate': 'transactions', 'pipeline': pipeline, 'explain': True}) (lines ~47-48).

checks.practice: Create the indexes the application needs before inserting the sample data (ensure indexes are created in the seed script prior to data writes).
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py main() calls ensure_indexes(db) then seed(db) (lines ~56-59).

checks.practice: Read optional external API keys (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY) from the environment and only invoke external services when the key is present to keep optional dependencies conditional.
checks.evidence: src/detector.py reads OPENAI_API_KEY via os.getenv and uses OpenAI only if present (lines ~13-16 and ~130-141).

checks.practice: Fail fast with a clear error if the required DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable is not set so the operator can supply configuration before runtime.
checks.evidence: src/db.py get_client() raises EnvironmentError if DOCUMENTDB_URI is not set (lines ~13-17).

checks.practice: Place $match early in aggregation pipelines (before expensive stages) and use projection; validate heavy pipelines with explain to avoid long-running scans.
checks.evidence: src/detector.py pipeline starts with {'$match': {'from_account': start_account}} (line ~35) and includes projection (line ~44). supports_graph_lookup uses explain (src/db.py line ~48).

checks.practice: Design transaction documents with explicit fields used by detectors (from_account, to_account, timestamp, amount, and a consistent _id) to support deterministic queries and joins.
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py constructs transactions with _id, amount, timestamp, from_account, to_account (lines ~33-46).

checks.practice: Use timestamp sorting and explicit time-window queries (ranges) when checking for rapid pass-through behavior.
checks.evidence: src/detector.py computes in_time and queries for outgoing tx within timedelta(minutes=15) (lines ~97-104).

checks.practice: Use replace_one(..., upsert=True) for idempotent writes when seeding or when a retried operation should not create duplicates.
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py uses db.transactions.replace_one({'_id': doc['_id']}, doc, upsert=True) when inserting transactions (lines ~47-49).

checks.practice: Include an example connection string showing SSL/TLS options (e.g., ssl=true) in .env.example to indicate TLS should be used in production connections.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example includes a commented example with ssl=true (lines ~2-4).

checks.practice: If an aggregation operator may be unavailable on the server, use explain rather than running the pipeline to validate operator acceptance without executing heavy work.
checks.evidence: src/db.py uses {'explain':True} in the aggregate command to validate $graphLookup (lines ~47-48).

checks.practice: Keep optional external integrations conditional (check for API key presence at runtime) and fall back to local deterministic templates if the external LLM is not available.
checks.evidence: src/detector.py uses OPENAI_API_KEY conditional and falls back to templated narrative if OpenAI call fails (lines ~13-16, ~131-148).

checks.practice: Use a unique index on accounts.account_id to enforce uniqueness for account lookup and to support deterministic traversal starting points.
checks.evidence: src/seed_data.py creates acc.create_index([('account_id', ASCENDING)], unique=True, name='idx_account_id') (lines ~12-13).

decision_reviews.comment: Approval with readiness 'ready_with_gaps' is an operator action. The decision is recorded and consistent with the build/run events.
Choice of Python 3.13 is supported by the environment and reflected in the build logs (events show Python 3.13 on PATH).

Choice of PyMongo (pymongo==4.4) is implemented in code and requirements.txt. The decision's reason_source is 'model_default' (the implementer selected a reasonable default); consider documenting the chosen driver/version in README for discoverability.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment is implemented (src/db.py lines ~13-19) and correctly recorded.
Attempting $graphLookup then falling back is implemented: supports_graph_lookup in src/db.py and follow_chain in src/detector.py. Events show the check and fallback were executed during runs.

Optional OpenAI summarization is implemented conditionally. The reason_source is 'model_default' (a default design choice); it is defensible but would benefit from a README note describing how narratives are generated and which OpenAI versions were tested.

The decision to skip pytest is recorded with reason_source 'tool_unavailable' and the events show pytest was not on PATH (events.jsonl). The alternative (installing pytest) was available but the run exercised the main scripts directly instead.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Guidance in public docs or an explicit sample-level rule advising that a single MongoClient instance should be created and reused for the life of the process (module-level client or cached factory).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local code only (documentation_search_available=false). I inspected src/db.py, src/seed_data.py, src/run_detector.py.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample constructs a new MongoClient in get_client() each call; this is functional but not optimal for connection pooling and can lead to extra connections.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short rule in the agent kit: 'Create and reuse a single MongoClient per process; expose get_client() that returns a cached client. Example code snippet and rationale.'

doc_gaps.topic: Server feature and operator compatibility for DocumentDB
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative, discoverable guidance that states which MongoDB aggregation operators ($graphLookup, explain, server-side JS, etc.) and vector-index createIndex options the managed DocumentDB cluster supports and the exact parameter names/syntax.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local code and readiness notes; no external docs reachable (documentation_search_available=false).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Implementer added a runtime supports_graph_lookup check and a client-side fallback. Without official operator support docs, implementers must rely on runtime checks and cannot author guaranteed server-side pipelines or index creation snippets.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A small 'Feature matrix' page listing supported aggregation operators, the exact createIndex syntax for vector indexes and the recommended engine options and example commands tested against the validated cluster SKU; include an index-creation sample and an explain-based operator-test snippet.

doc_gaps.topic: Vector index parameters and embedding-dimension guidance
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Explicit, public guidance connecting embedding model output dimensions to the vector index 'dims' parameter and recommended HNSW/IVF/DiskANN tuning values for small sample datasets vs production.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repository and prior-belief searches recorded in discovery; external docs were not reachable (documentation_search_available=false).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample does not implement vector indexes; if vector search is added later, implementers will lack authoritative defaults to choose safe parameters or to tune them for recall/latency.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A page titled 'Vector search on Azure DocumentDB — dimensions and index tuning' that states: the tested embedding dimensions for recommended models, how to create indexes with exact `createIndex` fields, and suggested efConstruction/efSearch/nprobe equivalents for small vs large datasets.

doc_gaps.topic: Secrets best practices (Key Vault / managed identity)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Clear guidance for storing/rotating long-lived secrets (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY) in Azure Key Vault and how to use a managed identity for least-privilege access for data-plane where supported.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repository, readiness notes; external docs not reachable.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Sample correctly avoids committing secrets but provides only .env-based usage. Operators may expect a recommended production path to Key Vault/managed identity.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Short 'Secrets & production config' page showing (1) example of reading secrets from Azure Key Vault using DefaultAzureCredential where supported, (2) fallback to env var for local dev, (3) explanation of which data-plane auth methods are supported for the validated cluster SKU.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A recommended pattern and example tests that run without a live cluster (e.g., using mongomock or patching MongoClient) so CI can run tests offline.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local tests and README; external docs not reachable.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Current test requires a live cluster and therefore will not run in an offline CI job; developers will be unable to get quick feedback without a cluster.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add 'tests_offline.md' and a small test module demonstrating how to patch the pymongo.MongoClient to use mongomock or a fake collection for unit tests; include a tox/pytest marker example.

doc_gaps.topic: Index and createIndex syntax for vector indexes (naming/disambiguation)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A clear, authoritative example showing exact createIndex keys and accepted parameter names for HNSW/IVF/DiskANN on the managed DocumentDB SKU (names and allowed ranges).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repo; no external docs available.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Without exact option names, a script that attempts to create vector indexes may fail at runtime on some SKUs.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A minimal 'create_vector_index.py' sample with validated syntax and annotated parameter descriptions for the supported index types; include a short README paragraph about compatibility caveats.
